summary: Older people talk about Social Security as a worry about retirement, in a modest voice, and do not want to be a burden.
realLife: At a roundtable ahead of an election, older residents spoke of their retirement worries in a modest voice. One had worked part-time while caring for a disabled son, held jobs without benefits and worried what she would get back from Social Security; another said she did not want to be a burden on her children. The seniors themselves were not quoted arguing about taxes; the campaigns carried that debate.
sources: https://www.wowt.com/2026/10/20/iowa-seniors-voice-fears-over-social-securitys-future-ahead-midterms/ (local TV report on a seniors roundtable)
gates: the speaker is of retirement age or near it
the speaker has paid payroll tax or has a benefit on record

whether the benefit is the largest part of income
